newsitem.title: USA: Barnett in card alliance with Household.
newsitem.headline: Barnett in card alliance with Household.

text.p: Barnett Banks Inc said Thursday it has signed a definitive agreement with Household Credit Services Inc to form a strategic alliance to build and manage Barnett's credit card business.
Household Credit Services is the credit card subsidiary of Chicago-based Household International Inc.

Barnett said it will sell to Household $780 million in non-core credit card receivables including accounts that are held by customers who live outside of Florida and Georgia, certain accounts of recently acquired credit card customers and other non-core accounts with lower credit scores.

Terms of the sale were not disclosed and Barnett said it will not recognize a material gain or loss on the sold portfolio. Barnett said it expects the transaction to be accretive to earnings per share in its first year.
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 1996.

Barnett said the alliance will expand its credit card business by building a portfolio that focuses on Barnett customer relationships and growth in the company's Florida and Georgia markets. The alliance will also manage and grow Barnett's existing $1 billion relationship portfolio, which is made up of cardholder accounts in Florida and Georgia.
Barnett said the alliance will seek to expand Barnett's credit card business by combining Household's marketing sophistication and servicing efficiency with Barnett's brand and market strength.

Under the agreement, Barnett cards will continue to carry the Barnett brand. Barnett and Household will actively market Barnett-branded cards to both current customers and potential customers, with the two companies sharing profits generated from the new portfolio.
"This transaction positions Barnett for profitable growth of its credit card portfolio while improving credit quality," said Charles Rice, Barnett chairman and chief executive in a statement.
